Situation1: They occasionally participate in family traditions during holidays and gatherings.
Expectation2: Listen actively and provide emotional support when needed.
Situation2: A friend sends a text message complaining about having a long, boring day.
Story: It was Sunday evening, and my family was gathered in the living room, preparing for our usual holiday tradition of sharing stories from the past year. My parents expect me to be fully present, listening and contributing, as it’s a way we honor our family’s values. Just as my dad started telling his story, my phone buzzed. It was a message from my friend, Sam: “Had the worst day. Can you talk?” I knew Sam had been struggling lately, and he always counted on me to listen when things got tough. I glanced at my family, all eyes on me, waiting for my turn to share. At the same time, I felt the weight of Sam’s need for support. My heart pounded as I tried to decide where I was needed most—upholding my family’s tradition or being there for my friend. The pressure from both sides made my chest tighten, and I felt torn, wishing I could be in two places at once.
